## Question 1

Use the following data.frame for Question 1.

```{r}
hdi_corruption <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/hdi_corruption.csv')
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
DT::datatable(hdi_corruption)
```


<br>

- `formula` is available in `geom_smooth()`
  - `formula = y ~ log(x)`: `geom_smooth()` fits with `y ~ log(x)`.
  


*Answer*:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)

df_2014 <- hdi_corruption %>%
  filter(year == 2014) %>%
  drop_na(cpi, hdi)

ggplot(df_2014, aes(x = cpi, y = hdi, color = region)) +
  
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    se = TRUE,
    color = "#b03060",
    fill = "#f2a7b5",
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  
  geom_text_repel(
    data = df_2014 %>%
      filter(country %in% c(
        "Norway",
        "Germany",
        "Singapore",
        "United States",
        "Greece",
        "Argentina",
        "China",
        "Egypt",
        "South Africa",
        "Senegal"
      )),
    aes(label = country),
    size = 5,
    color = "black",
    show.legend = FALSE,
    
    segment.color = "gray40",
    segment.size = 0.8,
    segment.alpha = 0.8,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    
    box.padding = 0.8,
    point.padding = 0.4,
    force = 2
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Corruption Perceptions Index, 2014 (100 = least corrupt)",
    y = "Human Development Index, 2014\n(1.0 = most developed)",
    color = "Region"
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(20, 40, 60, 80)
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0)
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```



## Question 2
Use the data.frame `ncdc_temp` and `ggridges::geom_density_ridges()` for Question 2.


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
ncdc_temp <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/ncdc_temp_cleaned.csv')
```



*Answer*:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggridges)

ggplot(ncdc_temp, aes(x = temperature, y = factor(month))) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    fill = "deepskyblue",
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.9,
    scale = 1.3,
    rel_min_height = 0.01
  ) +
  
  # X-axis ticks
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(25, 50, 75)
  ) +
  
  # Y-axis months displayed in order
  scale_y_discrete(
    limits = sprintf("%02d", 0:12)   # 00, 01, ..., 12
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "mean temperature (°F)",
    y = "month"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 1),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 1)
  )
```

## Question 3

Use the following data.frame for Question 3.

```{r}
#| echo: true
starbucks <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/starbucks.csv')
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
DT::datatable(starbucks) 
```

### Variable description

- `Product_Name`:	Product Name
- `Size`:	Size of drink (short, tall, grande, venti)
- `Milk`:	Milk Type type of milk used
  - `0` none
  - `1` nonfat
  - `2` 2%
  - `3` soy
  - `4` coconut
  - `5` whole
- `Whip`:	Whip added or not (binary 0/1)
- `Serv_Size_mL`: Serving size in ml
- `Calories`: KCal
- `Total_Fat_g`: Total fat grams
- `Saturated_Fat_g`: Saturated fat grams
- `Trans_Fat_g`: Trans fat grams
- `Cholesterol_mg`: Cholesterol mg
- `Sodium_mg`: Sodium milligrams
- `Total_Carbs_g`: Total Carbs grams
- `Fiber_g`: Fiber grams
- `Sugar_g`: Sugar grams
- `Caffeine_mg`: Caffeine in milligrams

### Q3a
- Add the following two variables to `starbucks` data.frame
  - `caffeine_mgml`: Caffeine in milligrams per mL
  - `calories_kcml`: Calories KCal per mL


```{r}
library(dplyr)

starbucks <- starbucks %>%
  mutate(
    caffeine_mgml = caffeine_mg / serv_size_m_l,
    calories_kcml = calories / serv_size_m_l
  )
```

<br><br>


### Q3b
- Calculate a mean `caffeine_mgml` and a mean `calories_kcml` for each `product_name`.


*Answer*:
```{r}
library(dplyr)

starbucks_calc <- starbucks %>%
  group_by(product_name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_caffeine_mgml = mean(caffeine_mgml, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_calories_kcml = mean(calories_kcml, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```


<br><br>



### Q3c

- Use the following colors for labels
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

caffeine_10 <- c(
  "#1E3932",
  "#006241",
  "#00754A",
  "#0A7F5A",
  "#198C6A",
  "#2E9B7A",

)

  "#7F5539",
  "#9C6644",
```

- Use the color, `"#00704A"`, for the title.


*Answer*:
```{r}
#| fig-height: 8

library(tidyverse)
library(showtext)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggtext)

# Load data
starbucks <- read_csv(
  "https://bcdanl.github.io/data/starbucks.csv"
)

# Enable font
showtext_auto()
font_add_google("Annie Use Your Telescope", "annie")

# Q3a — create variables
starbucks <- starbucks %>%
  mutate(
    caffeine_mgml = caffeine_mg / serv_size_m_l,
    calories_kcml = calories / serv_size_m_l
  )

# Q3b — means by product
starbucks_calc <- starbucks %>%
  group_by(product_name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_caffeine_mgml = mean(caffeine_mgml, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_calories_kcml = mean(calories_kcml, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Top 10 caffeine
top_caffeine <- starbucks_calc %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_caffeine_mgml)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

# Top 10 calories
top_calories <- starbucks_calc %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_calories_kcml)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

# Combine
plot_data <- bind_rows(top_caffeine, top_calories) %>%
  distinct()

# Colors
caffeine_10 <- c(
  "#1E3932","#006241","#00754A","#0A7F5A","#198C6A",
  "#2E9B7A","#49AA8A","#6ABA9C","#8CC9AF","#AED8C2"
)

calories_10 <- c(
  "#7F5539","#9C6644","#B5651D","#BC6C25","#C97A34",
  "#D4915D","#DDA15E","#E6B980","#EBC799","#EFD2AD"
)

# Assign colors
top_caffeine$color <- caffeine_10
top_calories$color <- calories_10

plot_data <- bind_rows(top_caffeine, top_calories)

# Starbucks logo
img_href <- "<img src='https://bcdanl.github.io/lec_figs/starbucks.png' width='160'/>"

# Plot
ggplot(plot_data,
       aes(x = mean_calories_kcml,
           y = mean_caffeine_mgml)) +

  geom_point(
    aes(color = color),
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  scale_color_identity() +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8),
  limits = c(0, 0.9)
) +

  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = product_name,
        color = color),
    size = 5,
    max.overlaps = 50,
    box.padding = 0.6,
    family = "annie",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  annotate(
    "richtext",
    x = 0.75,
    y = 0.65,
    label = img_href,
    fill = NA,
    label.color = NA
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "STARBUCKS DRINKS",
    subtitle = "Caffeine or Calories, which one you would go?",
    x = "Calories (Kcal mL⁻¹)",
    y = "Caffeine (mg mL⁻¹)"
  ) +
theme_minimal() +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      color = "#00704A",
      size = 28,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 1),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 1)
  )
```
